===== WORLD 21 · LESSON tilt_and_variance · Tilt and variance =====

TASK w21_1_teach [theory] What is an actionable sign of tilt?
CAPTION: Tilt is a state that changes how you decide. Track the decision step that slipped. A loss or win can prompt a check, and the check measures behavior.
TEACH: What is an actionable sign of tilt? Tilt is a state that changes how you decide. Track the decision step that slipped. A loss or win can prompt a check, and the check measures behavior.
Q: What is an actionable sign of tilt?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REASONING: principle decision_quality_signals · alt alternative · edge processRule · stack_matters unknown · assumption none
  + [correct] You start skipping the range or price check you normally perform — Correct. A skipped decision step is observable and can trigger your planned pause.
  - [wrong] You lost one large hand — Look again. A sound decision can still lose. Inspect your process for a change.
    BETTER ANSWER: You start skipping the range or price check you normally perform
  - [wrong] You won the last two pots — Look again. Wins can precede winner’s tilt, but the result itself does not establish a process failure.
    BETTER ANSWER: You start skipping the range or price check you normally perform

===== WORLD 21 · LESSON structure_and_stopping · Structure and stopping =====

TASK w21_2_teach [theory] How should time and condition rules interact when either is enough to stop?
CAPTION: Plan a warm-up, a focused playing block and a review. Set a time limit and a condition-based rule ahead of play. Stop-win can protect a player who reliably loses focus while ahead.
TEACH: How should time and condition rules interact when either is enough to stop? Plan a warm-up, a focused playing block and a review. Set a time limit and a condition-based rule ahead of play. Stop-win can protect a player who reliably loses focus while ahead.
Q: How should time and condition rules interact when either is enough to stop?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] End when the first stopping condition is met — Correct. The time limit protects against drift. The behavior rule can end the block earlier.
  - [wrong] Wait for both conditions — Look again. The written policy treats each condition as sufficient.
    BETTER ANSWER: End when the first stopping condition is met
  - [wrong] Delay until session profit returns to zero — Look again. The stopping reason is session quality or time, not making the result look different.
    BETTER ANSWER: End when the first stopping condition is met

===== WORLD 21 · LESSON table_selection_and_reciprocality · Table selection and reciprocality =====

TASK w21_3_teach [theory] What matters when deciding whether to remain at a table?
CAPTION: Table selection means choosing a game based on the current seats, opponent skill and your own attention. Reciprocality asks how the other player could profit from the same flaw you are looking for.
TEACH: What matters when deciding whether to remain at a table? Table selection means choosing a game based on the current seats, opponent skill and your own attention. Reciprocality asks how the other player could profit from the same flaw you are looking for.
Q: What matters when deciding whether to remain at a table?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The current lineup, position and your present decision quality — Correct. A normally beatable game can be a poor choice when the lineup or your focus has shifted.
  - [wrong] Whether the table was soft an hour ago — Look again. Seats and conditions can change. Reassess the current game.
    BETTER ANSWER: The current lineup, position and your present decision quality
  - [wrong] Whether leaving proves you lost strategically — Look again. Leaving a bad game can be the action with better expected value.
    BETTER ANSWER: The current lineup, position and your present decision quality

===== WORLD 22 · LESSON equilibrium_and_matrix · Equilibrium and matrix =====

TASK w22_2_teach [theory] What does a best response hold fixed?
CAPTION: A strategy matrix gives payoffs for all combinations of policies in an abstract game. At equilibrium neither side gains by deviating alone. A balanced strategy is a way of choosing actions that limits what opponents can gain by adjusting to your patterns. Ties between actions can support a mix.
TEACH: What does a best response hold fixed? A strategy matrix gives payoffs for all combinations of policies in an abstract game. At equilibrium neither side gains by deviating alone. A balanced strategy is a way of choosing actions that limits what opponents can gain by adjusting to your patterns. Ties between actions can support a mix.
Q: What does a best response hold fixed?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The other player’s strategy — Correct. Choose your action or probabilities to maximize payoff against that policy.
  - [wrong] Your own strategy while changing theirs — Look again. That evaluates the other player’s counter, not yours.
    BETTER ANSWER: The other player’s strategy
  - [wrong] The hand result from one played line — Look again. Expected payoff spans all outcome branches.
    BETTER ANSWER: The other player’s strategy

===== WORLD 22 · LESSON frequencies_and_regret · Frequencies and regret =====

TASK w22_3_teach [theory] What does “this hand bets 60%” say?
CAPTION: A frequency is a probability over repeated opportunities with the relevant hand or range. Regret compares a chosen sequence’s payoff with an alternative fixed action against the observed responses.
TEACH: What does “this hand bets 60%” say? A frequency is a probability over repeated opportunities with the relevant hand or range. Regret compares a chosen sequence’s payoff with an alternative fixed action against the observed responses.
Q: What does “this hand bets 60%” say?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] When this hand reaches this node, betting is selected on 60% of repeated trials — Correct. The denominator is opportunities for the specified hand at the node.
  - [wrong] The bet size is 60% of the pot — Look again. A selection frequency and a bet amount describe different properties.
    BETTER ANSWER: When this hand reaches this node, betting is selected on 60% of repeated trials
  - [wrong] Bet against 60% of the opponent’s holdings using a pure betting strategy — Look again. The frequency refers to your action given the information available.
    BETTER ANSWER: When this hand reaches this node, betting is selected on 60% of repeated trials
